visualReview.notes: All 11 current portable frames inspected: preview, four turntables, southwest clock, northeast rear, clock/trifora, open marble belfry, roof plan and far silhouette. Corrected whole-tower framing contains the 84 m tip and ground. Lower alternating brick/tuff courses, recessed openings, Roman clock relief, four open triforas, terrace rails, octagonal two-light belfry, bell frames and low metal roof remain intact.

sharedSurfaceReview.notes: All 11 current shared-surface frames inspected under sky-PMREM lighting, including the north-up mapped placement. Seven material graphs retain metric courses and raw stone, marble, painted metal, concrete, timber and copper surfaces. The clock, slender columns, open arches and bells remain legible. Geographic loading, material sharing and distant unload assertions passed.

geographicReview.notes: Exact Q1819804 OSM way138829597 supplies the 9.04 by 9.27 m shaft anchor and axes. Operator rooftop photographs from Palazzo Maffei show the clock on the southwest facade, establishing the directed phase; native +Z faces southwest rather than taking an arbitrary rectangular-axis sign. The north-up placement capture confirms the mapped shaft with the expected projecting cornices and terraces. Ordinary host terrain supplies ground contact. Connected Palazzo della Ragione wings and Arco della Costa remain separate surrounding buildings.

fidelityReview.notes: Passed for the detailed permanent exterior reconstruction. Operator history and municipal records establish 84 m total height, the 37 m original alternating brick/tuff shaft, fifteenth-century octagonal belfry and 1795 clock. Current operator photographs establish course rhythm, upper window phases, four open triforas, balconies/corbels, marble paired belfry bays, four bells and low metal roof. The campanology measurement establishes the 1.831 m Rengo bell diameter. Intermediate level heights, minor mouldings, individual voussoirs, secondary bell sizes and static clock display are explicit proportional reconstructions; interior rooms and the adjacent palace are outside this exterior asset scope.
